correctness.rationale: For integer m,N>=1 on normalized-area complex harmonic Bergman space, the orthonormal Fourier monomials e_k are shifted by T_m=P_h M_{z^m} with explicit positive weights derived from the radial moment 1/(q+1). The all-positive weights are bounded away from zero for fixed m, giving invertible contraction, forward norm1. For a length-N forward shift path staying on one side of zero, squared weight products telescope; crossing paths have reciprocal square F_{a,b}(j) proportional to [(am+j+1)(bm+m-j+1)]/[(j+1)^2(m-j+1)^2]. Its log second derivative is strictly positive on j∈[0,m], so crossing-residue maxima occur only at actual endpoint paths. The exact maximum is max_{0<=t<=N}(mt+1)(m(N-t)+1), attained only for balanced integers; the inverse INPUT (terminal of forward path) modes are e_{m floor N/2}, e_{m ceil N/2}. Thus ||T_m^{-N}||² equals the balanced product with dimension one for even N and two for odd N. Compact perturbation of m bilateral shifts plus spectral-radius bounds yields unit-circle spectrum, linear inverse norm slope m/2. Independently computed exact rational Fourier weights and inverse products for 72 parameter pairs with correct norming indices. This bounded check supplements, but does not replace, strict log convexity proof.
